findings.reason: yargs-parser.ts:984 now calls hasFlagsMatching(arg, flagWithEquals, negatedBoolean, normalFlag) without checking configuration['boolean-negation']. negatedBoolean (line 112) captures `foo`, so hasAnyFlag is true, isUnknownOptionAsArg returns false and pushPositional at line 226 is skipped. The negation branch at line 253 still requires boolean-negation, so the arg falls through to the long-option branch at line 261 and sets `no-foo`. Both reviewers traced the same path. I kept Claude's high severity over Codex's medium because this silently changes parse output for an existing configuration combination.
findings.claim: isUnknownOption now always matches the negatedBoolean pattern, even when boolean-negation is disabled. With unknown-options-as-args on and boolean-negation off, `--no-foo` for a registered `foo` is parsed as an option named `no-foo` instead of being passed through to argv._.
findings.evidence: The diff removes `if (configuration['boolean-negation']) patterns.push(negatedBoolean);` and replaces it with an unconditional `hasFlagsMatching(arg, flagWithEquals, negatedBoolean, normalFlag)`. `negatedBoolean` (line 112) captures `foo` from `--no-foo`, and `hasAnyFlag('foo')` returns true for a configured `foo`. The parse loop applies negation only when `configuration['boolean-negation']` is set (line 253), so the unknown-option check and the parse logic now disagree.

findings.reason: The only test that sets 'boolean-negation': false (test/yargs-parser.mjs:2536) does not enable unknown-options-as-args. None of the unknown-options-as-args tests (lines 3036-4160) disable boolean-negation, so nothing exercises the changed branch.
findings.claim: No test covers unknown-options-as-args together with boolean-negation: false, so the regression passes the suite.
findings.evidence: Searching test/ for a test that sets both `boolean-negation` and `unknown-options-as-args` finds no matches.
